title: guardEvidence recognizes file evidence from both filesystem and git history
context: guardEvidence distinguishes literal backslash bytes (legal POSIX filename chars) from Windows path separators to prevent false misroute refusals. The prior check (filesystem presence only) failed for deleted files: a file gone from disk but known to git would pass through un-normalized, then be misread as a separator by downstream code. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Added namesRealEvidence(root, f) to check both filesystem presence (isFile) and git history (pathKnownToHistory). guardEvidence now treats a relative entry as real evidence if either check passes, grounding truth in both current state and historical git knowledge.
consequences: Deleted files with literal backslash bytes are correctly preserved (not normalized), fixing false refusals on valid deletes
Absolute paths to backslash-byte files in sibling worktrees are now correctly flagged as misroutes (previously silently produced no candidates — a false negative)
guardEvidence gains durability across file lifetime: the same evidence entry is handled correctly whether the file currently exists on disk or is only known to git history
alternatives_rejected: Filesystem-only check (prior approach) — fails for deleted files and misses absolute-path sibling-worktree cases
Always normalize through toPosixTarget — destroys the ability to distinguish and preserve literal backslash bytes
Consult only git history — would miss current files that don't yet have history or ignore disk-only artifacts
